meta.title: Steerpost: publish to social networks, for you and your AI agents
meta.description: Connect your social accounts, compose once, schedule per platform, and let AI agents help through a scoped MCP server. Try the demo in your browser.
meta.ogAlt: Steerpost. The human steers. The agent posts.
hero.lead: Self-hosted publishing to {liveCount} networks. Agents draft through MCP; publishing, deleting and disconnecting wait for your approval.
hero.alt: The Steerpost composer with a post written for LinkedIn and Telegram.
hero.caption: Recorded in the live demo.
strip.title: Publishes today to
how.title: Draft, approve, publish
how.1.title: Your agent drafts
how.1.text: Create an MCP connection and paste its config into your agent. By default, it can only read and draft.
how.1.alt: The MCP connections page with a permission picker and a ready-to-paste client config.
how.2.title: You approve the risky part
how.2.text: Publishing now, deleting and disconnecting wait in Approvals until you say yes. Each approval works once.
how.2.alt: The Approvals page listing a request from an MCP agent to publish a post now, with Deny and Approve buttons.
how.3.title: Steerpost posts it once
how.3.text: Posts go out on time. If Steerpost cannot tell whether one went out, it marks it for you to check.
how.3.alt: The calendar in month view with draft, scheduled, published and failed posts.
look.title: Or do it yourself
look.a.alt: The composer with account chips, custom text per account and live previews.
look.a.cap: Compose. One post, custom text per network, live previews.
look.b.alt: The Steerpost dashboard: connected accounts, scheduled and published counts, upcoming posts, drafts, recent posts and failures.
look.b.cap: Dashboard. What goes out next, and what failed.
look.c.alt: The accounts page with connected networks and the others marked as not available.
look.c.cap: Accounts. What each network supports, and what it does not.
mcp.title: Agents work within limits you set
mcp.f1: Scoped keys. An agent sees only the tools its key allows.
mcp.f2: Approvals. Publish now, delete and disconnect wait for your yes, unless you mark the key as trusted.
mcp.f3: Revocable. Revoke a connection, and its key stops working at once.
mcp.f4: Audited. Every agent action is in the audit log.
mcp.paste: Create a connection under Developer, then paste its config:
mcp.ask: Then ask: “Draft a post about our new release for LinkedIn and Telegram.”
mcp.tools: All {toolCount} tools, each tied to one scope
mcp.setup: Setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor: <mcpdocs>MCP docs</mcpdocs>.
rel.title: Built so a post goes out once
rel.1.title: No double posts
rel.1.text: If a crash hides the result, the post is marked unconfirmed instead of sent again.
rel.2.title: Safe retries only
rel.2.text: Network errors and rate limits retry up to {retryCount, plural, one {# time} other {# times}}. Other errors fail with the reason.
rel.3.title: Secrets stay secret
rel.3.text: Network tokens are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and never logged.
rel.4.title: No lost schedules
rel.4.text: The database is the source of truth, so a Redis restart loses no scheduled post.
net.title: Where it publishes, and where it does not
net.linkedin: Personal profile. Text, up to 20 images, delete. No video yet.
net.telegram: Channels and groups. Text, images, video, delete.
net.discord: A channel webhook. Text, up to 10 images, delete.
net.mastodon: Any compatible server. Text, images, delete.
net.bluesky: App password. Text, up to 4 images, delete.
net.review: Need app review or a paid API
run.title: Run it yourself
run.text: One command starts the whole stack. Turn on the test network to try it without credentials.
final.title: See it work first
final.text: The demo runs in your browser, with sample posts, accounts and agents.
footer.text: Self-hosted social publishing for people and their AI agents. The demo runs entirely in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere, and this site has no trackers.
